text:
maria-support: Customer in EU reports live-streaming connection that runs for ~20-25s then abruptly returns a 401 when their client reconnects to our standby region (they see it only during a reconnection attempt). They provided an httpie snippet; I converted it but can't reproduce from my laptop.

jamal-engr: paste the httpie + your curl. also ask for the trace id from customer logs (x-request-id / trace-id) — we need to search auth and gateway logs.

maria-support: here's their httpie (sanitized):
```
http --stream POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat Authorization:"Bearer <TOKEN>" Accept:text/event-stream model=="rwd-stream-1" <<< '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"check stream"}]}'
```
my local curl I tried:
```
curl -N -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-stream-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"check stream"}]}'
```
I didn't see the 401. customer trace-id: eu-recon-44321

oliver-sre: Ask them to run a verbose, byte-level curl and save stdout/stderr. Provide them a single command they can paste. Important flags: --no-buffer, -v, --http1.1 (rule out HTTP/2 muxing on proxies), --trace-ascii for timing details. Also add an X-Request-ID with their trace-id so we can correlate.

Suggested command to send them (drop-in, they should not paste tokens into ticket):
```
# run once against primary, once against standby (or force client reconnect)
curl --no-buffer -v --http1.1 --trace-ascii trace.txt \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: eu-recon-44321" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  --data-binary @- > raw.output 2> raw.stderr <<'PAYLOAD'
{"model":"rwd-stream-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"check stream"}]}
PAYLOAD
```

jamal-engr: Instruct them to run it twice: 1) normal run, 2) while forcing a reconnection to standby (either by switching their client or pointing to a standby hostname). We need both raw.output/raw.stderr and trace.txt. If they redact the token, fine. If they attach partial headers, include raw.stderr to preserve server headers.

eva-ml: Also request they try adding `--header 'Connection: close'` in a separate run. If a reconnection path or proxy is dropping Authorization on a re-POST it might be visible with that variation. And ask them to try `--expect100-timeout 0` for proxies that buffer.

maria-support: I'll paste these steps in the ticket. Checklist for customer (pasteable):

1) Run the verbose curl above, save both files (raw.output, raw.stderr, trace.txt). Run once against their normal endpoint and once while simulating a failover reconnection to standby. Attach all files.
2) Do NOT paste the Authorization token into the ticket. Attach files as uploads (we can redact server-side if needed). If they must show headers, they can replace the token with <REDACTED>.
3) Include the exact local timestamp and timezone for the run and the trace-id (eu-recon-44321).
4) If using a corporate proxy or load balancer, include `env | grep -i proxy` output and any proxy config. Also include client logs that show when the underlying TCP socket closed and reopened.
5) Optional: run a packet capture (tcpdump) or ngrep if they can and attach pcap.gz. Only do this if they consent and remove any PII.

ops-bot: Automessage: ticket #SUP-4987 created and initial logs attached.

jamal-engr: Once we have the files, search gateway and auth logs for X-Request-ID: eu-recon-44321 in both eu-west-1 and eu-west-2, and look for any 302/307 or 401 responses upstream. Also check if any intermediate 5xx preceded the 401.

oliver-sre: If we can't reproduce, ask for a short packet capture centered on the 20s window (start capture 10s before the stream and keep for 40s). Also ask them to capture client reconnection attempt logs — the exact timing is crucial.

maria-support: Customer replied and uploaded raw.output/raw.stderr (token redacted). They saw the stream run ~22s then an in-stream `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="auth"` in the headers. Uploading to ticket and flagging eng.

jamal-engr: grabbing now. If we can't reproduce in eu-west-1, check the auth-service rotation logs and our edge token cache TTLs. Could be a short window where a session revocation or token-introspection call failed during cross-region failover.

maria-support: I'll follow up requesting a pcap if eng asks. Thanks team :thumbsup:
